commit.message:
paraLLEl-GS: Take device memory from GSVulkanHeap

Granite's device memory allocator and the arena code under it are gone;
its DeviceAllocator is now a thin layer over the core's heap, the one
the Vulkan renderer uses. The heap gains what paraLLEl-GS relied on,
all off unless asked for: memory priority classes kept in blocks of
their own, allocate flags for buffer blocks (device addresses), dedicated
memory given back when its object goes, and a per-memory-heap limit,
set to the budget of a small PCI BAR heap so buffers fall back to host
memory instead of overrunning it. Block slots take their first spans
from a pool made at init, so a block taken during play allocates
nothing on the host, for either renderer. Image memory aliasing, which
nothing used, is gone too.

tests/vkheap covers the additions and that nothing is chained when they
are off; tests/pgslog fails if Granite's allocator comes back.
